where: archway at the end of the upper path
desc: The main dirt path leads under an archway where deep shadows make it visually ambiguous whether the route continues forward or ends at a wall.

verify.why: The archway is illuminated by hanging lanterns, making the passage clearly visible and readable to players.

where: central pathway archway and market structure
desc: Heavy shadow and dense structure clutter make it ambiguous whether the main path continues through the gate or is blocked.

verify.why: The main pathway through the central gate is wide and visually clear, framed by lit lanterns to guide player navigation.

where: lower-left shadowed pit under the main platform
desc: Pitch-black shadow under the lower walkway makes it impossible to see if the ground below is walkable or a lethal drop.

verify.why: The lower-left pit contains visible barrels, lighting, and floor geometry rather than pitch-black occlusion.

desc: Deep shadows and overlapping roofs completely block the view of the ground path connecting the left settlement area to the right platform.

verify.why: The central walkway and its railing are brightly lit by sunlight and clearly visible connecting the areas.

desc: A harsh, pitch-black shadow cuts across the central pathway, completely obscuring ground details and making navigation unreadable.

verify.why: The shadowed central ground area is lit by ambient light, making the dirt texture and path details completely visible.

desc: A massive tilted green roof in the immediate foreground blocks the player's view of the path and space underneath it.

verify.why: Foreground structures framing the bottom of an environmental render are standard compositional elements rather than a visual bug.

desc: The large foreground roof structure obstructs the camera view of the paths and lower platform beneath it.

verify.why: Using foreground architecture to frame a scene render is a standard artistic technique rather than a flawed view obstruction.

desc: A large foreground roof completely occludes the lower ground level, hiding potential paths and hazards beneath it.

verify.why: The foreground roof serves as deliberate compositional framing for the environmental view rather than an improper occlusion flaw.

itemWhat: the way out of this area on foot towards loop-stairs — a path that carries on out of the frame
desc: the way out of this area on foot towards loop-stairs: ABSENT — There is no identifiable path or exit leading towards loop-stairs visible in this frame.

verify.why: The blocky carved staircase on the lower right of the cliff face is plainly visible as a descending exit path.

desc: The environment abruptly ends into a pitch-black unrendered void at the left boundary of the map.

verify.why: The dark top-left background represents the atmospheric shadow of the cave ceiling rather than an unrendered void.

where: underneath the central wooden stilts and platforms
desc: Harsh, unlit pitch-black shadows beneath the platform obscure the terrain, making it impossible to tell if there is an accessible lower route.

verify.why: Terrain, foliage, and water under the central wooden stilts are illuminated and clearly visible rather than hidden in pitch-black shadows.

where: stilt structures and walkways in lower center
desc: Harsh shadows and dense overlapping stilt supports completely obscure lower paths and ground level, making navigation difficult.

verify.why: The ground and water beneath the stilt supports remain visible between the posts, so lower areas are not completely obscured.

where: boat on wooden rails at bottom center
desc: The boat sits perfectly upright on wooden tracks without any side cradles or supports to keep it from tipping over.

verify.why: Placing a boat prop directly on tracks without custom side cradles is standard for stylized environment art and does not negatively impact gameplay.

where: wooden scaffold framework in the upper middle background
desc: The wooden scaffolding consists of disjointed, floating beams that fail to connect to the cliff face or surrounding platforms.

verify.why: The framework in the upper middle background is a connected, stilt-supported wooden structure rather than floating disjointed geometry.

desc: The central circular platform is completely enclosed by a railing, leaving no clear entrance or walkable route onto it.

verify.why: The railing only borders the front edge facing the water, leaving the sides and rear of the platform completely open and walkable.

desc: The wooden skeleton frame appears disconnected and floating without clear structural anchoring to the cliff or platform below.

verify.why: The upper center framework is anchored to the posts and platforms beneath it as part of the intended construction style.

desc: Visual clutter and overlapping wooden roofs make it difficult to tell which surfaces are walkable paths versus non-traversable roofs.

verify.why: The central circular platform is flat, open, and visually distinct from surrounding roofs, making its walkable nature clear.

where: wooden stilt support area in upper-left center
desc: The dense cluster of dark wooden stilts, platforms, and deep shadows makes the navigable path leading up into the village hard to read.

verify.why: The dark stilts are structural supports under the raised buildings rather than a player walkway, which is routed via the stairs on the left.

where: end of wooden boardwalk on the right
desc: The main wooden walkway leads directly into a wall/cliff under a low platform on the right, leaving the continuing path unclear.

verify.why: The walkway simply functions as a dock terminating at the rocky shore, which is expected layout for a waterfront pier.

desc: The dense layer of wooden ramps, platforms, and broken dock planks blends together in shadow, making it difficult to discern which surfaces are walkable.

verify.why: The central walkways and docks are well-lit by multiple lantern light sources and ambient light, rather than being obscured or hidden in shadow.
